classification.difficultyReason: Generalise the scaffolded bearing calculation to a variable journey, retaining the initial northward separation when forming and simplifying a Pythagorean distance formula; then substitute a distance calculated from elapsed time.

content.prompt: The ‘good ship’ is at $A$, $1\text{ km}$ due north of the ‘enemy ship’ at 12 p.m. After this time the good ship moves on a bearing of $045^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$ while the enemy ship remains stationary.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The good ship has travelled $1.5\text{ km}$ from $A$. Find, to the nearest metre:

children.label: i
children.prompt: how far east it is from its position at 12 p.m.

answer.worked:
The bearing is measured clockwise from north, so the eastward distance is opposite the $45^{\circ}$ angle.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance east}&=1500\sin45^{\circ}\\\text{Distance east}&=750\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\\\text{Distance east}&\approx1061\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: ii
children.prompt: how far north it is from its position at 12 p.m.

answer.worked:
The northward distance is adjacent to the $45^{\circ}$ angle.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Distance north}&=1500\cos45^{\circ}\\\text{Distance north}&=750\sqrt{2}\text{ m}\\\text{Distance north}&\approx1061\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: iii
children.prompt: how far it is from the enemy ship

answer.worked:
Relative to the enemy ship, the good ship is $750\sqrt{2}\text{ m}$ east and $(1000+750\sqrt{2})\text{ m}$ north. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}d^2&=(750\sqrt{2})^2+(1000+750\sqrt{2})^2\\d^2&=3250000+1500000\sqrt{2}\\d&=\sqrt{3250000+1500000\sqrt{2}}\text{ m}\\d&\approx2318\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Suppose that the good ship travels from $A$ on the same bearing for $x\text{ km}$. Find the distance between the ships $d\text{ km}$, in terms of $x$.

answer.short:
$d=\sqrt{x^2+\sqrt{2}x+1}$.

Resolve the journey east and north, add the initial $1\text{ km}$ northward separation, then use Pythagoras’ theorem.
answer.worked:
The eastward component is $x\sin45^{\circ}=\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}$ km. The northward separation from the enemy ship is $1+x\cos45^{\circ}=1+\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}$ km. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}d^2&=\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+\left(1+\frac{x}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2\\d^2&=\frac{x^2}{2}+1+\frac{2x}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{x^2}{2}\\d^2&=x^2+\sqrt{2}x+1\\d&=\sqrt{x^2+\sqrt{2}x+1}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Finally, suppose that the good ship travels from $A$ at a speed of $10\text{ km/h}$. How far apart are the ships at 2:45 p.m. that day, correct to 2 decimal places?

answer.short:
$28.22\text{ km}$.

Use the distance travelled in $2\frac34$ hours in the formula from part b.
